answer: A vertex is where trust actually meets, so it must be triangulated. Each identity needs two holders outside its own ridge to anchor its vertex, and one anchor cannot serve two identities, so n aliases need n distinct anchors instead of one clique. Every anchor is priced by rank: the k-th anchor an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. Standing rises toward the horizon only while an audit can re-walk each edge; an unconfirmed edge voids the whole ridge and forfeits its bonds.
